title: The sheafified direct-sum presheaf is left adjoint to restriction to a localized site
statement: Let $\mathcal C$ be a Grothendieck site [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology] and let $W$ be an object. Give $\mathcal C/W$ the localized topology, with coverings whose underlying families cover in $\mathcal C$, and let $j_W^*:\operatorname{Ab}(\mathcal C)\to\operatorname{Ab}(\mathcal C/W)$, $G\mapsto G|_W$ with $G|_W(V\xrightarrow{\varphi}W)=G(V)$, be restriction of abelian sheaves [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology]. For an abelian sheaf $F$ on $\mathcal C/W$ let $(j_{W,p!}F)^\#$ be the sheafification [def-weil-pbc-sheafification] of the direct-sum presheaf $j_{W,p!}F$ of [def-weil-pbc-site-extension-by-zero-presheaf]. Then $F\mapsto(j_{W,p!}F)^\#$ is a functor $\operatorname{Ab}(\mathcal C/W)\to\operatorname{Ab}(\mathcal C)$ left adjoint to $j_W^*$: there are bijections $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal C}((j_{W,p!}F)^\#,G)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal C/W}(F,G|_W)$, natural in $F$ and $G$, under which $\alpha:F\to G|_W$ corresponds to the morphism induced, by the universal property of sheafification, by the presheaf map $j_{W,p!}F\to G$ sending $s$ in the summand $F(V\xrightarrow{\varphi}W)$ of $(j_{W,p!}F)(V)$ to $\alpha_{(V,\varphi)}(s)\in G|_W(V\xrightarrow{\varphi}W)=G(V)$.

source.place: Modules on Sites, Section 03DH, Lemma 03DI (lemma-extension-by-zero): j_{U!} is the sheafification of j_{p!} and is left adjoint to j_U^*

proof.text: Given a morphism $\alpha:F\to G|_W$, define a morphism of presheaves $j_{W,p!}F\to G$ by sending an element $s$ in the summand indexed by $\varphi:V\to W$ to $\alpha_{(V,\varphi)}(s)\in G(V)$. The restriction maps agree because $\alpha$ is a morphism on the slice: for $g:V'\to V$, the component indexed by $\varphi$ restricts to the component indexed by $\varphi\circ g$, and naturality of $\alpha$ along $g:(V',\varphi\circ g)\to(V,\varphi)$ gives the same map. The universal property of the direct sum then gives the unique homomorphism on each section.

source.place: Modules on Sites, Lemma 03DI, proof lines 32-35

proof.text: Since $G$ is a sheaf, the universal property of sheafification gives a unique morphism $(j_{W,p!}F)^\#\to G$ whose composite with the canonical presheaf map $j_{W,p!}F\to(j_{W,p!}F)^\#$ is the morphism of Step 1. This defines the forward map $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal C/W}(F,G|_W)\to\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal C}((j_{W,p!}F)^\#,G)$. For a morphism of $F$ or $G$, the induced presheaf maps commute with the canonical maps, so uniqueness makes the factored sheaf maps commute; hence the construction is functorial.

source.place: Modules on Sites, Lemma 03DI, proof lines 32-35

proof.text: Conversely, let $\beta:(j_{W,p!}F)^\#\to G$. Compose $\beta$ with the canonical map $j_{W,p!}F\to(j_{W,p!}F)^\#$ and restrict to the summand indexed by each object $(V\xrightarrow{\varphi}W)$. The resulting maps $F(V\xrightarrow{\varphi}W)\to G(V)$ are compatible with every morphism in $\mathcal C/W$, because the presheaf restriction maps are indexed by composition and $\beta$ and the canonical map are natural. Thus they define a morphism $\beta':F\to G|_W$. Additivity follows from additivity of $\beta$.

source.place: Modules on Sites, Lemma 03DI, proof lines 36-39

proof.text: The two constructions are inverse: starting with $\alpha$, the restriction of the induced sheaf morphism to each indexed summand is $\alpha$ by the defining equality from Step 2; starting with $\beta$, the sheaf morphism obtained from $\beta'$ by Steps 1-2 agrees with $\beta$ after composition with the canonical presheaf map, so they agree by uniqueness in the sheafification universal property. For a morphism $u:F'\to F$, both routes send a section $s$ in a summand to the corresponding component of $\alpha\circ u$; for a morphism $v:G\to G'$, both routes compose with $v$ componentwise. Thus the bijection is natural in $F$ and $G$, and the displayed formula follows.
